uses.issue: Core statutory ground: whether post-9 June 1952 subletting, assignment, or parting with possession occurred without the landlord's written consent.
uses.law_quote: without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord;
uses.reason: This is the supplied Delhi provision that directly defines the fixed eviction ground. The record contains opposing positions on exclusive possession, licence versus subletting, and whether the 1944 lease or later conduct supplied written consent.
uses.standalone_value: Supplies the threshold elements and the 9 June 1952 temporal boundary, but does not itself resolve whether respondents had exclusive possession, whether the transaction was a licence, or whether a qualifying written consent existed.
uses.incremental_value: It is the anchor for evaluating section 16's lawfulness rules and the supplied Delhi precedents on assignment/parting with possession; other units cannot displace its express written-consent requirement without a demonstrated applicable override.
uses.limits: Current Indian Kanoon statutory reproduction; historical version is unverified, other section 14 grounds are excluded, and no target judicial interpretation is embedded in this unit.

uses.issue: How a company amalgamation may be characterized as a transfer of tenancy and why written consent can matter in a rent-control setting.
uses.reason: The Supreme Court treated a company-proposed amalgamation as transferring the tenant company's interest and possession under the Andhra Pradesh Act. That is contextual for the record's bank-amalgamation history, but it does not itself decide the Delhi ground or establish the legal mechanism of either bank amalgamation here.
uses.standalone_value: Supports only the general proposition that an amalgamation can operate as a tenancy transfer in the specific AP-law and scheme context before that Court.
uses.incremental_value: Adds an amalgamation-transfer analogy to the Delhi statutory text and reported Delhi precedent, but remains secondary because the target record does not identify a matching company-law mechanism or written-consent status for the bank successions.
uses.limits: Judicially adopted application under Andhra Pradesh law and a specific company amalgamation; not a Delhi holding and not proof of how Pratap Bank, Lakshmi Commercial Bank, or Canara Bank succeeded to this tenancy.

uses.issue: Scope of Delhi section 14(b) as extending beyond consensual subleases to assignment or other modes of parting with possession.
uses.reason: This Supreme Court passage reports a prior Delhi Rent Control Act holding that section 14(b) is broad enough to cover assignment or another mode of parting with possession, including an involuntary sale. It directly informs the statutory phrase relied on in the fixed question.
uses.standalone_value: Supports a broad reading of assignment/parting with possession under Delhi law, but does not determine whether these respondents' occupancy or the historical bank amalgamations fit that category.
uses.incremental_value: Extends the bare statutory wording of section 14(1)(b) by showing that transfer can be broader than a conventional sublease; it is especially relevant if bank succession is argued as an assignment route.
uses.limits: The unit is General Radio's report of Parasaram, not the independently supplied full Parasaram opinion; its factual setting involved liquidation sale, not these bank amalgamations or alleged occupancies.

uses.issue: Whether a protected tenancy/licensee status can pre-exist and survive later statutory acquisition in a different rent regime.
uses.reason: The unit concerns a Bombay Rent Act protected licensee and later statutory acquisition of Esso's interests. It provides context that succession consequences can depend on an independently created protected status and special acquisition statute, but the target record supplies no matching Bombay-law status or Esso-type acquisition.
uses.standalone_value: Shows only that, in its own statutory setting, an existing licence/protected-tenancy status materially affected the later vesting analysis.
uses.incremental_value: Helps limit overgeneralization from amalgamation cases by illustrating that tenancy succession may turn on the source statute and pre-existing status; it does not add a Delhi section 14(1)(b) element.
uses.limits: Bombay Rent Act and Esso acquisition context; no demonstrated application to the Delhi premises or the 1961/1985 bank successions.

uses.issue: Effect of an express special-statute vesting clause that makes a successor the lessee or tenant.
uses.reason: The unit shows a specific acquisition statute expressly vesting tenancy in government and then a government company. It is relevant context for distinguishing statutory succession from ordinary assignment, but the supplied record does not identify an equivalent vesting provision for either bank amalgamation.
uses.standalone_value: Supports tenancy succession only under the specific Esso Acquisition Act/Bombay Rent Act framework described.
uses.incremental_value: When read with the Delhi amalgamation materials, it shows why the precise legal source of a merger or vesting can matter; without a matching statute or scheme in the target record, it cannot resolve the fixed ground.
uses.limits: Specific Esso Acquisition Act, notification, section 396 amalgamation, and Bombay Rent Act section 15A; not a general Delhi eviction immunity.

uses.issue: Counter-position that court-ordered amalgamation vesting may occur without landlord consent and may fall outside section 14(1)(b), while the actual eviction issue remains reserved.

uses.reason: The Delhi High Court states a prima facie view favorable to vesting on amalgamation without landlord consent, but immediately says it is not deciding whether such transfer amounts to assignment attracting section 14(1)(b) and preserves the landlord's plea. uses.standalone_value: Supports only a provisional counterargument about amalgamation vesting and confirms that the section 14(1)(b) consequence requires decision in the proper rent-control proceeding.

uses.limits: Prima facie and expressly reserved; partial document, specific company-scheme context, and no showing that either target bank amalgamation used the same mechanism.

uses.issue: Possible statutory mechanism for voluntary amalgamation of banking companies and transfer/vesting under a sanctioned scheme.
uses.reason: Section 44A supplies one banking-law route by which a sanctioned amalgamation can bind the banks and transfer property and liabilities. Because the record merely states two historical amalgamations and does not identify section 44A or the governing schemes, the unit provides mechanism context only.
uses.standalone_value: Shows what section 44A can do for an amalgamation sanctioned under that section; it does not establish that the 1961 or 1985 target succession occurred under section 44A or transferred this lease on particular terms.
uses.incremental_value: Useful for testing whether an asserted bank succession rests on a statutory vesting mechanism rather than ordinary assignment, but it needs the actual historical scheme/order before it can affect section 14(1)(b).
uses.limits: Official consolidation as amended through a modern snapshot with historical version unverified; distinct from section 45 and from acquisition-act schemes.

uses.limits: Modern official consolidation with historical version unverified; actual scheme terms and historical applicability to the 1961/1985 bank amalgamations are absent.

uses.issue: Possible Central Government scheme power to amalgamate or transfer undertakings of corresponding new banks and vest assets and liabilities.

uses.limits: Historical version is unverified and OCR is uncorrected; the unit concerns corresponding new banks and does not itself identify the legal instrument used in the target bank history.
